summary: The analysis reveals a set of strong confounders, particularly those related to baseline health and oncology history (e.g., CKD stage, cholecystectomy history, clinical phenotype). A distinct group of pathological and clinical markers (e.g., CK5/6 expression, clinical decline, clinical severity score) act as effect modifiers, demonstrated by high support in causal forests and R-learners. Several features exhibit dual roles as both confounders and effect modifiers, reflecting their complex influence on both treatment assignment and the resulting outcome.
